what: R9 — 'a field half-edge may not lie on a city edge'. Gate artefacts for the DEFAULT-OFF flag CARCASSONNE_FIX_R9. Building the flag adopts nothing.
tile: city_top_straight_road (JCZ BA/RCr), x4 in the deck; the north farm region drops FarmerSide.TLT + FarmerSide.TRT, which lie on its city edge

seam.decision: process-global env flag, ONE python derivation, Rust consumes a codegen'd DELTA
seam.why: neither engine has a per-Game tile table (python `base_tiles` is an import-time module global; Rust `registry()` is a OnceLock), so a per-game flag is not available without a large refactor. The delta (`R9_FARM_OVERRIDE` in tiles/generated.rs) is codegen'd from `base_deck.r9_farm_override()`, so python<->Rust parity is structural rather than a hand transcription that has to be tested for.

flags_off_data_identity.note: regenerating generated.rs after the edit moved SOURCE_SHA256 only; SEMANTIC_DIGEST (everything the engine reads off a tile) is unchanged

effect_under_random_play.caveat: n=500, 1 event: the interval is very wide (~0.005%-1.1%) and this is RANDOM play, not champion play. The spike's 3.3% CONFIGURATION rate is the upper envelope of this; that the score-changing rate is strictly lower is exactly what it predicted. Champion play packs cities harder, so the production rate is plausibly higher. 0 games changed ply count => under this policy the flag never changed the legal-move sequence.

leaf_merge_measurement.question: the spike argued from shared tile data that flat_leaf / the Rust core reproduce the merge, but did not measure it
leaf_merge_measurement.answer: they do — all four implementations, both observables
leaf_merge_measurement.reproducer: two city_top_straight_road tiles, cities joined across the shared N/S border; the two under-city field strips
leaf_merge_measurement.score_fixture: the same board plus one more RCr east of the lower tile (a legitimate field join through a road edge); p0 has two farmers on the lower field, p1 one on the upper. Merged, p0 takes the completed city alone (+3); split, one each (0).
